text:
sam: Heads-up — after rolling driver 560.02 to the H100 fleet we started seeing the kernel-selector favor the small-seq slowpath. p95 token latency up ~18%, KV-cache hitrate down ~12% across Dedicated pools.

marco: Can you paste the profiler trace + the kernel picks? esp the tie-breaker values.

sam: quick snippet from last 5m sampling: 
```
kernel_selector: chosen=slow_small_seq_v2, score=0.82, tie_breaker=0.0003
previous: chosen=fast_small_seq, score=0.81, tie_breaker=0.0001
kv_cache: hitrate=0.68 -> 0.56
batching: avg_batch=3.1 -> 2.9
latency_p95=42ms -> 50ms
```

jess: aha, tie_breaker entropy increased after the driver bump. Looks like heuristics that rely on micro-bench kernels (warp sched timing) are noisy now.

carmen: Ops saw a spike in kernel-switch counts per-second too? That would explain cache churn.

sam: yes, kernel-switch events/sec ~x3 in the same window. I pushed a trace to https://perf.internal/runs/2389 — includes raw nvprof samples.

marco: Two possible mitigations: 1) force a model-level kernel override to pin `fast_small_seq` for the most latency-sensitive routes, 2) revert driver to 559.xx on affected nodes.

jess: I'd add a third: tighten tie-breaker threshold and add hysteresis in selector so it needs sustained advantage to flip. That avoids flip-flopping with noisy micro-benchmarks.

sam: Good. Proposed immediate ops plan: canary rollback of driver on 10% of Dedicated capacity -> measure p95/KV-hitrate for 30m. If good, roll back remaining. Also config patch to selector to increase tie-breaker weight from 1e-4 -> 5e-4 and enable 60s hysteresis.

carmen: Ops canize: `kubectl label nodes h100-dedicated-canary=driver559` and siphon traffic via routing policy. I can run the rollback playbook.

ops-bot: @carmen initiated canary rollback job 238912 on 2 nodes. status: pending. :gear:

ci-bot: smoke test: generate/latency route -> baseline p95: 41ms, post-driver p95: 50ms. Awaiting canary results.

marco: Also open a follow-up fix for autotuner: add a fallback that prefers kernels with stable batch/kvcache locality when hitrate drops > 8% in a sliding window. That will be a runtime flag.

jess: Agree. For the immediate hotfix I can push a config toggleset: `selector.tie_breaker_min=5e-4` `selector.hysteresis_sec=60` `selector.stability_bias=0.3` and roll that as a config-only rollout (no driver change) so we can test without infra-level rollback.

sam: Pushed config PR and linked it in perf run. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/4123

carmen: Canary rollback completed on 2 nodes — ops-bot shows those nodes running driver 559.89 again.

ops-bot: canary job 238912 finished: success.

ci-bot: canary metrics: p95 on canary nodes = 42ms, kv-hitrate = 0.67. Cluster-wide still degraded until we roll further.

marco: Good signal. Two-step: A) roll config toggleset to all nodes (non-disruptive) B) schedule phased driver rollback for next 3 maintenance windows if customers need it.

jess: Note: config toggleset reduced flip rate but didn't fully restore hitrate on all routes (some heavy chat routes still ~6% low). We'll monitor.

sam: Will run a targetted eval set against chat-heavy routes and report back in 45m. If we still see >8% kv drop, start scheduled rollback.

carmen: tagging @oncall for schedule. Also adding a temporary guardrail to routing policy: prefer nodes with driver 559.* for latency-critical routes until further notice.

marco: Action items: 1) sam — perf eval + logs (45m). 2) jess — land config toggleset and watch. 3) carmen — prep rollback windows and routing guardrail. 4) runtime team — start autotuner bug that adds hysteresis + stability bias.

sam: +1. I'll post the eval results in this thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:
